title: Count Matches
statement: Given an array of strings `items` and a string `ruleKey` and a string `ruleValue`, return the number of items that match the rule. Each item is represented as "type color name" (exactly three words separated by single spaces). The ruleKey can be "type", "color", or "name", and you should return the count of items whose corresponding part equals ruleValue.

examples.input: ["phone blue pixel", "computer silver lenovo", "phone gold iphone"], "type", "phone"
examples.explanation: The first and third items have type "phone".

constraints: All strings consist of lowercase English letters only.

title: Sum Multiples
statement: Given an integer `n`, return the sum of all integers in the range `[1, n]` that are divisible by 3 or 5.

examples.explanation: Numbers divisible by 3 or 5 are 3, 5, 6, 9, 10 and their sum is 33.

title: Find the Difference
statement: You are given two strings `s` and `t`. String `t` is generated by randomly shuffling string `s` and then adding one additional character at a random position. Return the letter that was added.

examples.explanation: The character 'e' is the one that was added.

constraints: `s` and `t` consist of lowercase English letters.
